t: The compound was likely begun by Rakai Pikatan and inaugurated by King Lokapala, and the Shivagrha inscription of 856 describes a Shiva temple compound resembling Prambanan.
It served as the royal temple of the Mataram kingdom, was abandoned around the middle of the 10th century, and fell into ruin after a major earthquake in the 16th century.
Dutch colonial restoration began in the 1930s, the main Shiva temple was completed in 1953 and the central temples by 1993, but only six of the 224 pervara temples have been fully rebuilt.
dyk: According to the Shivagrha inscription, a public water project moved the course of a river near the temple during its construction; the river is identified as the Opak, which now runs along the western side of the compound.
ev: The Shiva temple was inaugurated, according to the Shivagrha inscription issued by King Lokapala
The Javanese court was moved to East Java by Mpu Sindok, and the temples were abandoned around the middle of the 10th century
The temples collapsed in a major earthquake
Cornelis Antonie Lons, a VOC employee, gave the first report on the ruins in his journal
Nicolaus Engelhard commissioned H.C. Cornelius to clear, measure and draw the site, the first effort to study and restore it
The reconstruction of the main Shiva temple was completed and inaugurated by President Sukarno
The main temples of the central zone were complete and inaugurated by President Suharto
The Abhiṣeka ceremony was held for the first time, to cleanse and sanctify the temple as a focus of Hindu worship

f.made: Likely begun by Rakai Pikatan and inaugurated by his successor King Lokapala of the Mataram kingdom, then expanded by Balitung Maha Sambu and later Mataram kings such as Daksa and Tulodong
f.form: A Hindu temple compound on a square plan of three walled zones, once with 240 temple structures; the central Shiva temple is 47 metres tall and 34 metres wide, and Brahma and Vishnu temples are 33 metres tall
f.where: In the Special Region of Yogyakarta, southern Java, Indonesia, about 17 kilometres northeast of Yogyakarta, on the boundary with Central Java; a UNESCO World Heritage Site
f.known: the tall central Shiva temple; Ramayana and Bhagavata Purana bas-reliefs; 224 ancillary pervara temples in four rows; the Rara Jonggrang legend; anastylosis reconstruction; Ramayana ballet on full moon nights
